summary:
Design layer (fabless accelerator designers, EDA/IP vendors, plus referenced foundry/memory/OSAT/ODM suppliers) verification, full pass: 28/28 sources fetched and assessed (15 SEC 10-K/10-Q/20-F/8-K filings, 11 company press releases/blogs/product pages, 2 US government documents). 153 evidence items checked across companies, facilities (incl. capacity), flows, financial_links and controls -- all 153 verified verbatim against the primary document; zero quote_not_found, does_not_support, or superseded findings. 89 entity verdicts issued: 25 companies (all publish -- see note below), 20 facilities (17 publish, 3 publish_flagged for country-level precision on aggregated regional operations with no named site: NVIDIA Israel, Marvell Israel, Marvell India), 31 flows (30 publish, 1 publish_flagged -- TSMC->NVIDIA CoWoS, correctly labeled 'inferred' with a sound inference_note), 10 financial_links (all publish_flagged -- see below), 3 controls (all publish). Zero rejections.

Note on company verdicts: COUNSEL.md's procedure says entity_verdicts should cover companies 'only if their evidence is bad,' but the schema's own framing ('Nothing without your publish or publish_flagged verdict appears') and scripts/validate.mjs's behavior (every un-verdicted entity, companies included, is flagged 'will not be published') are both unconditional -- there is no company-specific exemption in the build path today. Since every company's evidence held up, I added a brief pass-through 'publish' verdict for all 25 rather than let well-sourced companies (NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom, Marvell, Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, OpenAI, Huawei, Arm, Synopsys, Cadence, TSMC, Samsung, SK hynix, Micron, GlobalFoundries, Amkor, ASE, SPIL, KYEC, Tongfu Microelectronics, Foxconn, Wistron) silently vanish from the atlas for want of a one-line verdict. None required in-depth scrutiny beyond what's already reflected in evidence_checks, consistent with the 'only if bad' spirit of the instruction.

Specific concerns addressed:
1. The seven quotes from pages that resisted raw download (Micron-AMD MI350 HBM release, OpenAI-Broadcom GlobeNewswire release, Meta MTIA blog 'TSMC 5nm' table cell) were all re-fetched this session. Micron and GlobeNewswire still blocked plain curl (Cloudflare challenge / connection reset respectively, consistent with the analyst's original note) but were independently re-verified via a live fetch-and-render tool, both confirming verbatim matches. The Meta blog was retrieved as raw HTML directly this time (no block encountered), and the raw markup confirms 'TSMC 5nm' sits immediately after the 'Technology' label in the 'Next Gen MTIA' spec card -- an exact match, not a paraphrase or OCR artifact. All seven quotes verified.
2. The ten purchase-commitment/prepayment financial_links (NVIDIA x4, AMD x3, Broadcom x1, Marvell x2) all connect a designer to a named supplier without a disclosed per-supplier dollar split. Descriptions were checked line by line: none contain an 'amount' field, and each description explicitly states the aggregate figure is Tier-1-sourced while the per-supplier share is undisclosed.
